title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The transcription line 'deg. tr. k(β)/K = u' must read deg. tr. k(β)/k = u, which is consistent with the field diagram (k(β) at most u over k).

There is a minor ambiguity over which group Q is a torsor under. P' ≃ Q ×^{H'} G' with H' = inverse image of Im j' in B' would give dim Q = u+1, whereas the claimed trdeg k(β)/k = u requires Q to be a U'-torsor, i.e. splittings inducing the identity on gr. The two readings can be reconciled only up to the central G_m/Tate twist; this is not spelled out.

The equality trdeg_k K = g+u implicitly requires that the only algebraic relations between periods and their complex conjugates are those coming from the torsor structure together with the real structure. Nothing on the page justifies why complex conjugation contributes exactly u new transcendentals. It is a conjecture, but the heuristic (that Q(ℂ)-coordinates are 'generic' in a U'-torsor) is only implicit.
The note on (2πi)^{±1} assumes the Tate objects lie in the category; otherwise the dimension count g includes no weight torus. This is not reconciled with the dimension bookkeeping.

ideas.what: Three period torsors P, P', P'' between Betti, de Rham and Hodge-graded fibre functors, with canonical complex points α, β, γ satisfying γβα = 1
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor / torsor of comparison isomorphisms (extended to the Hodge-graded fibre functor)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period torsor, via André's exposition); Deligne (tannakian formalism)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's period conjecture is stated in a footnote of 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) and developed by André (Une introduction aux motifs, 2004); the triangle including T_Hdg is not standard

ideas.what: Grothendieck period conjecture: trdeg k(α)/k = dim G for k ⊂ ℚ̄
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1960s), formulated by André, Bertolin, Kontsevich–Zagier
ideas.where_published: Footnote in IHES 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966)

ideas.what: Hodge filtration as a ⊗-filtration with parabolic stabilizer B', unipotent radical U', Levi quotient L', central Tate cocharacter j; Levi splittings ↔ lifts of j
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian filtrations (Saavedra), Hodge cocharacter, Mumford–Tate parabolic

ideas.what: Varieties Fil (⊗-filtrations of T_B of Hodge type, a flag variety G/B) and Big (Hodge-type bigradings, G/L), with Big→Fil a unipotent torsor
ideas.modern_name: Compact dual of a Mumford–Tate domain and the space of Hodge decompositions G/L (real-algebraic model of the MT domain)

ideas.what: Consequence: trdeg ℚ(φ)/ℚ = dim G/B for the period point of a motive over ℚ̄
ideas.modern_name: Generalized Schneider theorem / transcendence of period points (period point is generic in the Mumford–Tate compact dual)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schneider (1937) for elliptic curves; Cohen and Shiga–Wolfart (1990s) for 'algebraic period point iff CM'

ideas.what: Strong transcendence conjecture: trdeg_k k(α,β) = g + u, i.e. periods together with the Hodge decomposition (hence complex conjugates of periods) generate a field of transcendence degree dim G + dim U'
ideas.modern_name: Period conjecture enriched with real structure / Hodge splitting (related to single-valued periods)

ideas.what: Consequence trdeg ℚ(ψ)/ℚ = g − l for the Hodge-decomposition point (for elliptic curves: τ and τ̄ algebraically independent when non-CM)
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic independence of the period point and its conjugate in the MT domain

missed.claim: A 'strong' form of the period conjecture that adds the Hodge decomposition β (equivalently, complex conjugates of periods) and predicts the exact transcendence degree g + dim U'. For elliptic curves over ℚ̄ without CM, it predicts that ω1, ω2, η1, η2 and their complex conjugates generate a field of transcendence degree 5.
missed.quote: Conj. de transcendance forte — Si k ⊂ Q̄, alors deg. tr. k(α,β)/k = g + u
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Standard formulations (André, Kontsevich–Zagier, Brown) treat periods without their complex conjugates. Brown's single-valued periods live in the field generated by periods and their conjugates, and this page gives a precise conjectural transcendence degree for that larger field in terms of the Hodge parabolic. That is a concrete, testable refinement that does not seem to be in the literature.

missed.claim: The period point φ in the compact dual (flag variety of ⊗-filtrations of Betti type) conjecturally has transcendence degree exactly dim G/B. The Hodge-decomposition point ψ ∈ G/L has transcendence degree dim G/L. Both points are deduced from the period torsor by fibre-dimension counts.
missed.quote: deg tr. Q(φ)/Q = g−b ; deg tr. Q(ψ)/Q = g−b+u = g−l
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This generalizes Schneider and Cohen/Shiga–Wolfart (period point algebraic iff CM) to an exact transcendence degree for arbitrary motives, phrased via Mumford–Tate parabolics. The ψ statement (independence of the period point and its conjugate) seems not to be formulated anywhere.

missed.claim: The page links tannakian period torsors, Mumford–Tate domains / flag varieties, and transcendence of special points in a single dimension count, with Schneider's theorem as the test case on the next page.
missed.quote: Big →p Fil fibration, faisant de B un torseur sur Fil, de groupe U_Fil ... Fil a des dim égale à dim G'/B'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the arithmetic analogue of the modern Ax–Schanuel and functional-transcendence picture for period maps (Bakker–Tsimerman). Here it is stated for special arithmetic points rather than functionally, years earlier.

deep.surprise_reason: The core period conjecture is known and attributed to Grothendieck. The explicit enhanced conjecture with the Hodge splitting (exact count g+u) and its consequences for the period point and its complex conjugate are a notable unpublished refinement I do not recognize from the literature. It is, however, a conjecture sketch rather than a result.
transcription_corrections: 'deg. tr. k(β)/K = u' should be 'deg. tr. k(β)/k = u'.
'K = Q(k(α), k(α))' probably reads K = k(α, ᾱ) or similar (field generated by k(α) and its complex conjugate); the struck-out text is illegible.
'Big = Bigr_⊗ T_B ... de la [-bigr-] bigraduation de T_DR' should read: struck word replaced, class of the Hodge bigrading.

In the field diagram, the edge labels are: K over k(γ), k(α) at most u; K over k(β) at most g; k(ψ) under k(γ) at most l; k(φ) under k(α) at most b; k(β) over k at most u; k(ψ) over k(φ) at most u; k(φ) over k at most g−b; ℚ(φ) over ℚ at most g−b; ℚ(φ_1) over ℚ algebraic.
'Q ⊂ P' = Isom(T_DR,T_Hdg) ≃ Q ×^{H'} G'' is correct as read (P' is induced from Q).
